title: The weekend
goal: Tell and rate your weekend, while tackling the trickiest part of the past tense: where the little words — *mă, te, se, îl, o, îmi* — go once the helper *am, ai, a* joins the sentence.
bekal: use reflexive verbs in the past: *m-am trezit, te-ai culcat, ne-am plimbat*
place object pronouns correctly: *l-am văzut*, but *am văzut-o*; and *mi-a plăcut*
rate an experience: *a fost minunat, obositor, plictisitor*

notes: **M-am trezit.** In the present you say *mă trezesc*; in the past *mă* meets *am*, and since two vowels collide, the *ă* drops: *mă + am → m-am*. The hyphen isn't decoration — it marks exactly where a letter went missing, and the two words are read as one syllable: mahm.

**L-am văzut, but am văzut-o.** This is the promise from unit 12. Almost all the little pronouns attach **before** the helper (*îl + am → l-am*), except one: *o* (her/it, feminine) moves **after the participle**. *Hanul* (n, acting as m) → *l-am văzut*; *Maria* (f) → *am văzut-o*. Misplacing *o* is the classic learner's mistake, so drill this pair until it's automatic.

**Ți-a plăcut? — Mi-a plăcut.** The dative pronouns from unit 10 shorten too: *îmi → mi-*, *îți → ți-*. The subject is still the thing liked (*castelul*), so the helper is *a*, not *am* or *ai*. If the thing liked is plural, the helper follows: *Mi-au plăcut munții.*

**Sâmbătă without an article** = this past (or coming) Saturday, once. *Sâmbăta* with the article = every Saturday. ***Pe la** zece* = "around ten": *pe* before *la* blurs the time, very handy for casual stories.

**Prin Centrul Vechi.** *Prin* means "through" or "around inside": *ne-am plimbat prin parc, prin oraș, prin pădure*. Compare *la munte*, *la mare*, *la țară* — three holiday-destination chunks that never take an article.

grammars.title: Reflexives in the past — *m-am, te-ai, s-a, ne-am, v-ați, s-au*
body: The reflexive pronouns from unit 8 still stand in front, but now what follows them is a helper starting with a vowel. The result: pronouns ending in *-ă* lose that letter, and everything is joined with a hyphen.
after: **The rule in one line:** *mă, vă* drop the *ă*; *se* drops the *e*; *te* and *ne* stay whole. All are then hyphenated to the helper: *m-am, v-ați, s-a, s-au, te-ai, ne-am*.
**Negative:** just *nu* before the whole chain, with no further merging: *Nu m-am trezit la timp. Nu ne-am întâlnit. Andrei nu s-a culcat devreme.*

**A whole day in the past:** *M-am trezit la șapte, m-am spălat, m-am îmbrăcat și m-am dus la birou. Seara m-am uitat la un film și m-am culcat târziu.* All the routine verbs from unit 8 can now tell a story.
Plural reflexives often mean **each other**: *ne-am întâlnit* (we met each other), *ne-am văzut ieri* (we saw each other yesterday), *s-au cunoscut la Cluj* (they got to know each other in Cluj).

grammars.title: Object and dative pronouns in the past
body: The same rule applies to the accusative pronouns (unit 12) and the dative ones (unit 10): a leading *î* drops, a final *ă* drops, then a hyphen. The only rebel is *o*.

after: **Doubling with *pe* still applies**, exactly as in unit 12: *L-am văzut pe Andrei. Am văzut-o pe Ioana. I-am văzut pe colegi.* Negative: *Nu l-am văzut*, and for *o*: *N-am văzut-o.*

**Why does *o* go to the back?** Because *o am* would crash two vowels together with nothing that can drop. Romanian chose to move it instead. This happens only in this past tense; in the present *o* stays in front: *o văd → am văzut-o*.

**Irregular participles used so far** — learn them paired with the infinitive: *a fi → fost · a avea → avut · a face → făcut · a merge → mers · a vedea → văzut · a zice → zis · a scrie → scris · a pune → pus · a veni → venit · a bea → băut · a vrea → vrut · a putea → putut · a ști → știut · a da → dat · a lua → luat · a sta → stat · a rămâne → rămas · a deschide → deschis · a înțelege → înțeles*.

blocks.text: Try turning each line into the past with *eu*: *m-am plimbat prin oraș, am mers la munte, am făcut o excursie, am vizitat un muzeu, am ieșit în oraș, m-am întâlnit cu prietenii, am făcut curat, m-am odihnit, am dormit până târziu*. Watch out for *mare*: as a feminine noun it means "sea" (*la mare*), as an adjective "big" (*un oraș mare*). Context always tells them apart — *Marea este mare* = "The sea is big".

blocks.title: Where Bucharest escapes on weekends
items: **La munte.** The Prahova Valley — Sinaia, Bușteni, Predeal — is only about an hour and a half to two hours by train from Gara de Nord. Sinaia is home to *Castelul Peleș*, the summer palace built by King Carol I in the late 19th century.
**La mare.** From June to early September the main destination is the Black Sea coast: Constanța, Mamaia, and the more laid-back Vama Veche. You'll go there with Budi in unit 16.
**La țară.** Many city families still have grandparents in a village. *Merg la țară, la bunici* means coming back loaded with eggs, cheese, and jars of homemade *zacuscă*.
**La un grătar.** As soon as the weather warms up, Romanians fire up the grill: *mici*, meat, bread, and mustard. May 1 is practically national *grătar* day.

head: Sentence
English
rows: It was wonderful! · It was gorgeous!
It was tiring, but worth it.
I didn't like it at all.
*Mi-au plăcut munții, dar nu mi-a plăcut hotelul.*
I liked the mountains, but I didn't like the hotel.

blocks.text: Two small things make your verdict sound native. First, *a plăcea* still turns on the thing, not on you: one thing → *mi-**a** plăcut*, several things → *mi-**au** plăcut*. Second, before *mi-a, ți-a, l-am* the word *nu* does **not** merge — *nu mi-a plăcut, nu l-am văzut* — because the hyphen slot is already taken. The merged *n-am* only happens when *nu* meets the helper directly: *n-am văzut-o*.

blocks.title: Five Monday-morning questions
items: *Cum a fost în weekend?* — How was your weekend?
*Ce ai făcut sâmbătă?* — What did you do on Saturday?
*Unde ați fost?* · *Cu cine ai fost?* — Where did you go? · Who did you go with?
*V-ați distrat?* — Did you have fun? The typical answer: *Da, ne-am distrat de minune!*
*Te-ai odihnit?* — Did you get some rest? And almost everyone's honest answer: *Nu prea.* ("Not really.")
